blocks: Added vercel-labs/skills to my global toolchain. I'm just evaluating it at this point, but I suspect it can be used for declarative skills that are shared across multiple agentic coding tools. In that sense it's a bit duplicative of rulesync. I prefer how vercel has the ability to have symlinked .agents/skills to .claude/skills. I also like how it follows the "one thing well" philosophy. I could keep using rulesync for mcp and AGENTS.md synchronization, but maybe it's better to have a single purpose tool that manages AGENTS.md? Such a tool doesn't exist, at least as far as I know, but I haven't really searched hard for it.
https://1worldflag.com in particular, the shimmering transparent background version as the flag flies

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a pun on MCP — the Master Control Program — from the 1982 Tron movie, where MCP was the villainous AI that sought to dominate all computer programs
Skills can be bundled into an MCP/Server, making them available to any MCP client (not just Claude Code)
MCP/Server deployments that scale to zero need a token cache layer — e.g. Redis, KV, DynamoDB, or — since in-process token state is lost on each cold start
Async server-side agents calling protected APIs need Auth/M2M (client credentials / short-lived JWT) rather than user-delegated flows, since there is no human present to authorize
